title: Strong L2 compactness through possible contact for vanishing structural viscosity in periodic two-dimensional fluid–beam systems
source_title: On an existence theory for a fluid-beam problem encompassing possible contacts
author: Jean-Jérôme Casanova; Céline Grandmont; Matthieu Hillairet
difficulty_reason: The ordinary Aubin–Lions lemma does not apply directly to velocities on unknown moving domains when the limiting beam can contact the cavity bottom. The authors construct a source-specific lower interface and prove continuity of fractional-domain projections with the full cofactor/streamfunction construction, allowing projected time-derivative compactness on fixed domains. Their complete approximation-error and energy-pairing argument then gives strong fluid/beam velocity convergence through possible contact, rather than leaving the new contact geometry or projection closure to a reference.

proof_review.note: Full article retained as conservative closed context for notation, global assumptions, diagrams and references. Exact primary and supporting physical proof pages are recorded separately. Lemma18 in the Section3 vanishing structural viscosity construction: periodic two-dimensional incompressible viscous fluid under a one-dimensional elastic Euler–Bernoulli beam, positive fluid/structure densities and fluid viscosity, positive beam bending coefficient and nonnegative tension. Initial data satisfy2.11–2.14, including strictly positive initial gap and finite energy/divergence/normal-trace compatibility. For the authored gamma-positive damped approximations with regularized convergent initial data, a subsequence of (1_(F_hgamma)u_gamma,partial_t eta_gamma) converges strongly in L2 of the fixed space-time container times L2 of the beam to the corresponding undamped candidate velocities, permitting zero limiting gap/contact. Full new fractional-domain projection continuity16–23, uniform estimates and candidate construction24–28, lower-interface construction29–33, projected compactness and energy-pairing closure33–37 read. Necessary contact-space streamfunction/density9–12 and full authored density appendix37–39 read. Prior positive-viscosity global existence reference7, multiplier reference9 PropositionB.1, Rellich and the precise generalized Aubin–Lions statement reference5 are named existing background. Source intermediate scalar signs/labels in elementary change-of-variable estimates are retained; explicitly constructed cofactor pullbacks, lower interface and limiting pairing remain included. No independent contact/rebound law, uniqueness, nor general higher-dimensional fluid–shell assertion. Full global weak-existence theorem10 is not selected: its final interface trace coordinate display29 requires separate editorial clarification, while selected strong-compactness core does not use that display. Whole40-page original retained with actual JEP8(2021) DOI10.5802/jep.162 and pinned acquisition dates.
